nodes.statement:
Eight source-vs-paper discrepancies are recorded as open items rather
than silently resolved. params.yaml currently follows the CC3D
source-literal value in each numeric case, per the controller ruling
that the source is what actually produced the published figures — but
this is a recorded modeling choice, not a settled resolution, and is
carried forward as a decision_needed at the investigation level.

nodes.label: docs/cc3d-reference/sego2022-parameters.md §7 lists 8 places where the CC3D s...
nodes.statement: docs/cc3d-reference/sego2022-parameters.md §7 lists 8 places where the CC3D source and the paper's printed tables disagree: (1) neighbor order 3 (source) vs. an assumed 2 (paper silent), (2) Infected- Macrophage adhesion 20 (source, per-subtype) vs. the paper's collapsed "infected-immune = 10", (3) NKcell-CD8Tcell adhesion 25 (source) vs. the paper's collapsed heterotypic-immune = 10, (4) active lattice dimensions (175x175, source default) matching neither paper patch size exactly, (5) the initial-viral-load sweep {1,10,100,1000,10000} is scenario config, not enumerated in the source's base ModelInputs, (6) ViralCellDeathSteppable is an explicitly "simplified version" omitting the paper's printed ROS/viral-load Hill-saturation death term, (7) ContactKillingSteppable multiplies by cell_resist directly rather than (1 - cell_resist) like every other resistance consumer, (8) macrophage-virus chemotaxis is labeled "moderate" in the paper's table but numerically equals the "strong" NK value (5,000) in both source and paper — a qualitative-label mismatch, not a numeric one.

nodes.label:
New infections land significantly closer to already-infected cells
than unifo...
nodes.statement:
New infections land significantly closer to already-infected cells
than uniform-random placement would predict (~0.61x the chance
distance, discriminated against a per-update population-mean null
baseline, not a loose absolute radius) — spatial locality emerges from
the field's own diffusion length (25 sites) without any explicit
"infect-my-neighbor" rule in the transition itself, which only reads
local field concentration. A shuffled-field non-local control
correctly fails the same test (ratio ~1.13), confirming the locality
claim is genuinely earned rather than an artifact of a bound too loose
to discriminate.

nodes.statement:
With the IFN->resistance gate active, infected-cell growth is
slightly slower than the identical no-IFN path, but the effect is
WEAK at step 20 (only ~4% reduction, 2 cells) — not on its own strong
evidence of slowed spread. The gap widens meaningfully by step 40
(~23%) as the effect compounds, so this is a corroborating
directional trend that strengthens over time, not the study's primary
quantitative evidence (that's total_virus, F-02) and not a strong
signal at the step the underlying integration test actually asserts.

nodes.statement:
This is the study's PRIMARY, robust quantitative evidence. Gating
each infected cell's virus secretion by (1-resist) cuts total virus
roughly in half already at step 20 (~53% reduction, the step the
underlying integration test actually asserts) and stays in the
~53-58%-reduction regime through step 40 — a substantial, sustained
brake on virus load that is the direct, measurable output of the
resistance mechanism, and a much stronger signal at the tested step
than the n_I check (F-01).

nodes.label:
The resistance gate engages immediately (not a no-op) and stays
substantially...
nodes.statement:
The resistance gate engages immediately (not a no-op) and stays
substantially positive throughout, confirming the mechanism's
qualitative direction. It only PARTIALLY confirms the expected
behavior, though: resistance reaches a fast local steady state near
0.55 and stays essentially flat, rather than climbing toward
saturation (~1) as the naive expectation of "more IFN accumulates
over time -> more resistance" would suggest. This is flagged, not
hidden, as an Increment-9 calibration/convention open question (see
report.caveat and the standalone caveat item below).

nodes.statement:
The full fate lifecycle (infection H->I, infected death I->D, Allee
death/recovery H<->D, all wired together each update) composes into a
coherent, mass-conserving mechanism: the dead lesion grows steadily
over both a 200- and 500-update horizon, driven overwhelmingly by the
infection->death path (H->I->D), with population exactly conserved
throughout. This is the study's central confirming result.

nodes.statement:
Direct Allee death is honestly reported as essentially absent at this
reduced (0.3mm, ~900-cell) scale within practically-runnable step
counts. This is NOT hidden as a clean pass -- it is flagged (status:
partial) because it only PARTIALLY confirms the expected behavior
(the rate formula is verified genuinely positive-but-tiny at
qualifying encounters, ruling out a wiring bug, but the driver never
actually observes a death event). Structural causes (b_h/theta
asymmetry, per-update-vs-per-MCS batching) are recorded as an open
Increment-9 calibration question, not tuned away here.

nodes.label:
Placing BOTH the macrophage cluster and the infection in the domain
interior ...
nodes.statement:
Placing BOTH the macrophage cluster and the infection in the domain
interior (fix round 1, commit `4092d7c`) produces a genuinely
near-isotropic lambda=0 control -- small changes with no consistent
direction across seeds -- unlike the OLD corner-placed control, which
drifted with a strong, consistent bias (the confound the fix removed).
This confirms the localization in F-01 is caused by chemotaxis
specifically, not by wall-proximity drift, adhesion, or scenario
geometry alone.

nodes.statement:
The mean on/off gap exceeds the control's own noise floor (its
seed-to-seed spread), so the localization effect is not explainable by
control noise alone -- a direct, seed-by-seed paired comparison also
confirms chemotaxis-on beats chemotaxis-off in all 5/5 seeds, not just
on average. Together with F-01/F-02, this establishes the chemotaxis
mechanism is both necessary and sufficient for the observed
localization, and that the finding replicates across seeds rather than
being a single-seed artifact (the concern that fix round 1 addressed).

nodes.statement:
Both regulated IL-10 secretion pathways engage cleanly within a short
(15-update) run -- neither pinned at exactly 0 (the gate never opens)
nor saturating instantly (the gate is degenerate). The macrophage
pathway and the uninfected-cell pathway are independently gated
(Hill-self-regulation vs. 1-resist) but share the same underlying
Hill-constant plumbing (`sig_1`/`g_1`/`g_2`/`d_2`) that also gates
chemokine secretion (F-01), matching the source's shared-regulation
structure even though `sig_1` itself is a documented stub (see
caveats).

nodes.statement:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by F-04 (Task-9.3-review units fix, this update):
this finding originally reported extracellular_virus missing hardest
and identically at both loads (worst_miss ~1200) as a "units
mismatch" attributed to the engine's virus-field concentration scale.
That diagnosis was WRONG -- it was a structural raw-sum-vs-mean units
BUG in `repro_fig5`'s observable mapping (fixed, see F-04), not a
genuine PFU-equivalent calibration gap. With the bug fixed,
extracellular_virus is now among the BEST-matching observables (4/6
at load=1, FULLY in-band at load=10000), and the dominant remaining
miss driver is the population-count observables (infected_cells,
uninfected_cells) at load=1 -- the same population-scale (144 vs.
10000 cells) and run-duration (~0.068 vs. up to 15 simulated days)
mismatch `repro_fig3b`'s study documents for its own population
counts, not a units or PFU-scale issue. This is the study's honest
reported GAP (status: partial), not hidden behind the driver's
structural correctness (F-01/F-02): at reduced scale, per-load
`band_eval["passed"]` is still False for every tested load. load=10000's
uninfected_cells/antibodies/extracellular_virus land fully in-band, but
as `report.main_insight` documents this partly reflects the paper's
own widest, highest-spread bands at that load (Sec. 3.3) plus this
reduced run's near-instant total-infection collapse, not
individually-superior calibration at that load. NOT tuned away: no
constant was adjusted and `targets/fig5.json` was not edited to
narrow this gap.

UNITS FIX (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX): `repro_fig5` (and
`repro_fig3b`/`repro_...
nodes.statement:
UNITS FIX (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX): `repro_fig5` (and
`repro_fig3b`/`repro_fig7`) previously mapped `run_full_model`'s
"fields" section -- a RAW SUM of `world.field_conc(...)` over every
lattice site, needed as-is by the §4 ODE coupling's V/F/C/L inputs --
straight through to the field-typed target observables
(extracellular_virus, type1_ifn, chemokines, il10), while
`targets/{fig3b,fig5,fig7}.json` digitizes those as PER-SITE
CONCENTRATIONS (fig5.json's t=0 extracellular_virus target for
viral_load_multiplier=load IS load itself). The raw sum over-reports
by ~n_lattice_sites (structurally worse at paper scale, more lattice
sites), which is exactly what F-03 originally (mis)diagnosed as a
PFU-equivalent calibration gap. `_map_full_model_observables`
(`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py`) now converts only the 4
field-typed observables to the SPATIAL-MEAN concentration
(`sum(field_conc)/n_lattice_sites`, `n_lattice_sites` from this run's
own `params.dims`) at the repro-observable-mapping layer -- NOT in
`run_full_model`'s own recording, which Increments 0-8 and the ODE
coupling still rely on as a raw sum. This resolves the structural
sites-factor: extracellular_virus's worst_miss drops by ~4 orders of
magnitude at both tested loads, and load=10000's extracellular_virus
is now fully in-band (was 0/6). An HONEST RESIDUAL remains, NOT tuned
away: the spatial-mean model value at t=0 is consistently ~0.375x the
target at both loads -- the ratio of the seeded patch's lattice-site
count to the full simulation domain's lattice-site count
(`run_full_model` reserves margin/separation sites around the patch
for the immune-cell clusters and recruit reserve pool; the virus is
seeded only under the patch, so averaging over the larger full-domain
lattice dilutes it by the patch/domain area ratio). This is a
distinct, real domain-geometry effect, honestly flagged for Phase-B,
not evidence the units fix is incomplete, and no constant was tuned
and no band was widened to close it. Verified by the new fast
regression test
`test_repro_fig5_extracellular_virus_is_concentration_not_raw_sum`
(`tests/test_influenza_full_model.py`).

nodes.statement: extracellular_virus worst_miss: load=1 1199 -> 0.208, load=10000 1196 -> 0.0 (now fully in-band); t=0 spatial-mean model value ~0.375x target at both loads (e.g. load=1: mean=0.375 vs target=1.0; load=10000: mean=3750 vs target=10000), same order of magnitude

10000; only 2 of the paper's 4 infection fractions swept; ~0.068
simulated days vs. the target's 0.0-15-day checkpoint window),
per-fraction `band_eval["passed"]` is False for every tested
fraction. A NEW artifact beyond `repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b`'s
documented gaps: `round(0.001 * 144) = 0` -- the smallest tested
fraction seeds ZERO pre-infected cells at this reduced population, so
that run never experiences infection at all, driving its
uninfected_cells worst_miss to 2.29 (the largest of any
observable/fraction pair here) purely because the target expects
infection to emerge and partially recede, not because the mechanism
is wrong. Unlike `repro_fig5`'s ORIGINAL (now-fixed, see below)
extracellular_virus finding (a consistent ~1200x units-scale miss at
every tested load), fig7's extracellular_virus actually lands
mostly/fully in-band here (5/6 at frac=0.001, 6/6 at frac=0.05) --
this reduced run's near-zero/low virus-field magnitudes were never
near the sites-factor's regime, and this coincidence-of-scale reading
is unaffected by the units fix below. NOT tuned away: no constant was
adjusted and `targets/fig7.json` was not edited to narrow this gap.

UNITS FIX UPDATE (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX, this update): the
`repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b` "virus-field-units gap" this finding
deliberately left uninvestigated has now been diagnosed and fixed
(`repro-fig5-viral-load`'s F-04): it was a structural raw-sum-vs-mean
bug in the repro-observable mapping layer, not a genuine PFU-scale
calibration gap, fixed by reporting field observables as spatial-mean
concentration (`_map_full_model_observables`,
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py`). This study's OWN
extracellular_virus numbers above are CONFIRMED UNCHANGED by direct
re-measurement after the fix (byte-identical n_in/worst_miss at both
fractions) -- this finding's original read (a scale coincidence, not a
